newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's MPT not to take HK Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: China's MPT not to take HK Telecom stake.

text.p: China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunication (MPT) will not buy a direct stake in Hongkong Telecommunications Ltd, local media reported on Saturday.
"The MPT has no plans to buy shares in Hong Kong," China's Posts and Telecommunications minister Wu Jichuan was reported by the South China Morning Post as saying.
Hongkong Telecom's share price has risen in the past week on market anticipation that its parent Cable and Wireless Plc could sell a stake in Hongkong Telecom to China.
Wu declined to say whether the MPT would accept Cable & Wireless's majority 59 percent shareholding in Hongkong Telecom after the colony returns to Chinese rule on July 1.
"According to the International Telecommunications Union, telecommunications is a sector which represents the sovereign power of the state," Wu said.
"After Hong Kong is returned to the mainland (and) under the Basic Law, it is up to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to consider the management of telecommunications."

The minister was in Hong Kong to launch China Telecom (Hong Kong) Ltd, a joint venture between MPT-controlled China Telecom and Tianbo Communication (Holding), which would develop services in Hong Kong. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6358
